headline: Oil above $100 and surging yields push stocks into risk-off mode
body: Equities are in their third consecutive down session, with the S&P 500 off 0.5% to 7,636, the Nasdaq down 0.6% to 26,253, and the Dow shedding 0.8% to 52,381. The proximate trigger is crude oil: Brent has pushed back above $100 a barrel for the first time since July as tensions between the U.S. and Iran escalate in the Gulf, with reports of tanker strikes on both sides. Treasury yields have followed oil higher rather than acting as a safe-haven offset — the 10-year sits near 4.81% and the 30-year above 5.25%, both multi-year highs — a combination markets are reading as an inflation problem rather than a growth scare. The VIX is up about 5% to roughly 16.5, elevated but still well shy of stress-level readings.

Futures were steadier heading into Thursday, suggesting the selling looks more like a controlled repricing around energy and rates than a broad flight from risk — cautious rather than panicked. The one single-stock story cutting through the macro noise is Apple, which unveiled a foldable iPhone alongside pricier Pro models at a high-profile event; the stock still closed lower on the day even as the news drew attention, a sign the rates-and-oil worry is currently overriding company-specific catalysts. Retail chatter was thin in today's scan — no concrete wave of social-sentiment data to lean on — so this read leans more on price action and headline flow than positioning signals. With PPI and CPI due shortly, the next real test of the 'yields versus growth' narrative is close at hand.
